calculate the equations of tangent planes, and use them to approximate functions.
find the maxima and minima of functions of two variables.
apply the method of Lagrange multipliers to optimisation problems.

assessments.task_description:
You will submit solutions to a collection of mathematical problems at the end of your applied class.

The results from your best 6 exercises out of 12 will count towards your final grade.

A schedule for all of the weeks of semester will be provided on BlackBoard.
assessments.submission_guidelines: Worksheets will be submitted at the end of your applied class.
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.
assessments.late_submission: As noted under Extensions, assessment is completed within the scheduled class time and turned in at the end of the applied class. There are no late submissions as assessments are completed in class. Instead, students will drop the lowest six applied class assessment scores to account for absences due to illness or exceptional circumstances.

assessments.task_description:
The End of Semester Examination will be an in-person, paper-based exam for all students.

Internally enrolled students

The end-of-semester exam will be an in-person, paper-based exam. Students will sit the exam at the St Lucia Campus.

Externally enrolled students

The end-of-semester exam will be an in-person, paper-based exam. UQ Examinations will contact students directly to confirm arrangements. You will either sit the exam at the St Lucia campus (if you live within 200km radius of the campus) or will be directed to nominate an exam centre by a certain date. 

Please ensure you update your semester address in Si-net at the start of the semester.

One reminder will be sent and students who fail to nominate an exam centre will be automatically assigned to the St Lucia campus. Late nominations will not be accepted.

Lectures

Lectures will be delivered in a lecture theatre and streamed online. Topics include: Functions of several variables; Partial derivatives and tangent planes; Maximum and minimum problems on surfaces; Differential equations; Parametrisation of curves and line integrals.

learning_activities.topic:
Applied Classes

Each student should be enrolled in one applied class and attend the corresponding session twice each week. Applied classes provide students with the opportunity to discuss applied class and assignment problems with their peers and their casual academic. Applied Classes will begin in week 2.

Questions about other aspects of the course may also be asked during the applied classes, including the assignments, but work on assignments is to be individual work; other problems can be addressed as a group. During the applied classes, key exercises will be given to students to work through and solve collaboratively if they choose. The Applied Class Exercises (assessment) will be conducted and submitted during the applied classes.

Casual Academics are only available during applied classes. If you have questions about the course content at other times, refer to the Course Help section on the course Blackboard site, in particular look for information on the First Year Learning Centre.
